correctness.rationale: The exact F2 cubic coefficient domain of 1048575 forms, 35 lines, and six squarefree restriction masks is fully specified. Both separately implemented C++ and NumPy runs agree on all 840 rationally nonsingular eight-transversal forms and exclude every smaller candidate. Full PGL4(F2) orbit of mask 67194 has size 840 and equals the entire certificate, with 20160 group elements. Its four partials give a triangular absolute-smoothness proof. Therefore all 840 are genuinely geometrically smooth, and no smooth form has T<8. Actual scripts and outputs are embedded.

originality.rationale: The 2019 transverse-line paper proves asymptotic/sufficient field-size bounds, not a sharp q=2 cubic theorem; the inspected 2021 complete small-field cubic-surface taxonomy studies contained lines and configurations, not transverse exterior intersection counts. A direct, geometric equivalence/stronger-results search gave no coverage. Exact new interval and rigid orbit are not merely renamed prior results. A previously unindexed finite-field enumeration remains a publication-priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier arithmetic incidence computations might have evaluated transverse-line counts on the Dickson/Karaoğlu surface representatives.
The older 2021 equation lists make extraction straightforward, so publication priority requires external specialist confirmation; searches alone never certify uniqueness or novelty.
McKean's full paper was not inspected because its contained-line focus was not decisively relevant.

value.rationale: The sharp small-field Bertini invariant T(S) is a natural, coordinate-invariant finite-field line-section statistic, not an arbitrary subfamily enumeration. q=2 lies far below previously sufficient field-size criteria, and the unique extremal embedded type with projective stabilizer 24 captures unexpected rigidity. Full exact classification of the sharp boundary may support further arithmetic-geometric computations.
